LESSON: INTEGRATED FARMING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.3: Integrated Farming

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Integrated Farming. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can integrated farming conserve resources?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INTEGRATED FARMING
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Integrated Farming helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: INTEGRATED FARMING
Study Integrated Farming like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources

What this means
In this part you learn to describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Integrated Farming” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Integrated Farming is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Integrated Farming” around your school. (skill: describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Integrated Farming to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Integrated Farming from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Integrated Farming: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Integrated Farming?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can integrated farming conserve resources?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Integrated Farming means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe components of integrated farming in conserving resources.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
